subject: EVS
learning_goal: Master the chapter content using source-grounded explanations, practice and revision.

sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: Patterns with Threads Look closely around you.
sections.source_evidence: Patterns with Threads Look closely around you.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: Do you see birds building nests or spiders spinning webs?
sections.source_evidence: Do you see birds building nests or spiders spinning webs?

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: Nature is full of hidden artists — animals, birds and insects who weave, stitch, design, and even glue things together.
sections.source_evidence: Nature is full of hidden artists — animals, birds and insects who weave, stitch, design, and even glue things together.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: Did you know we have a hidden artist around us who has been weaving long before humans ever did?
sections.source_evidence: Did you know we have a hidden artist around us who has been weaving long before humans ever did?

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: Our Wondrous World 132 The Indian handloom sector employs over 45 lakh people, especially women and rural artisans, making it one of the largest cottage industries in the world.
sections.source_evidence: Our Wondrous World 132 The Indian handloom sector employs over 45 lakh people, especially women and rural artisans, making it one of the largest cottage industries in the world.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: The male baya weaver is a weaverbird, who builds beautiful hanging nests from grass.
sections.source_evidence: The male baya weaver is a weaverbird, who builds beautiful hanging nests from grass.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: They weave the strands over and under to make the nest strong.
sections.source_evidence: They weave the strands over and under to make the nest strong.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: The nest is shaped like a pouch and hangs from the branches of a tree.
sections.source_evidence: The nest is shaped like a pouch and hangs from the branches of a tree.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: The expert weaverbird weaves very fine nests, while the young ones who are just learning make rather rough ones.
sections.source_evidence: The expert weaverbird weaves very fine nests, while the young ones who are just learning make rather rough ones.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Weaving combines strips or threads of a material into a patterned fabric like cloth.
sections.source_evidence: Weaving combines strips or threads of a material into a patterned fabric like cloth.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: One set of thread is placed vertically and the other goes horizontally.
sections.source_evidence: One set of thread is placed vertically and the other goes horizontally.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: When these threads are carefully crossed over and under each other, they form a unified fabric such as a mat, a basket or many other things.
sections.source_evidence: When these threads are carefully crossed over and under each other, they form a unified fabric such as a mat, a basket or many other things.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: For a long time, people have been weaving many kinds of natural materials into mats, baskets or sheets from coconut fibre or palm reeds, bamboo, grass, jute and cotton or silk.
sections.source_evidence: For a long time, people have been weaving many kinds of natural materials into mats, baskets or sheets from coconut fibre or palm reeds, bamboo, grass, jute and cotton or silk.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: 133 Clothes — How Things are Made Discuss Have you seen products woven out of natural material at home or elsewhere?
sections.source_evidence: 133 Clothes — How Things are Made Discuss Have you seen products woven out of natural material at home or elsewhere?

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: Take 5 – 6 strips of blue paper and tape them at the top of a surface.
sections.source_evidence: Take 5 – 6 strips of blue paper and tape them at the top of a surface.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Take another set of yellow paper strips and weave them through — over, under, over, under.
sections.source_evidence: Take another set of yellow paper strips and weave them through — over, under, over, under.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: Can you use this method to make a basket?
sections.source_evidence: Can you use this method to make a basket?

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: Try using materials other than paper, such as strings, ropes, ribbons or reeds.
sections.source_evidence: Try using materials other than paper, such as strings, ropes, ribbons or reeds.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: Indian muslin was so fine that it was known as ‘woven air’ and a whole saree could pass through a ring.
sections.source_evidence: Indian muslin was so fine that it was known as ‘woven air’ and a whole saree could pass through a ring.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: Our Wondrous World 134 What can you find in your classroom that is woven?
sections.source_evidence: Our Wondrous World 134 What can you find in your classroom that is woven?
